meta.subject: Cross-Subject Construction Labs (Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Computer Science)

slides.title: C01 · Chemistry — Water Formation Equation
slides.purpose: Balance a foundational neutral molecular equation using whole-number coefficients without altering chemical subscripts.
onScreenText: Conservation of atoms: equal H and O on both sides
Adjust whole-number coefficients only — never change subscripts
Check simplest whole-number ratio (GCD = 1)

visual.description: Hydrogen and oxygen forming liquid water.
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eef2ff"/><text x="400" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="36" font-weight="bold" fill="#312e81">C01 · Water Formation</text><text x="400" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="24" fill="#4338ca">H₂(g) + O₂(g) → H₂O(l)</text></svg>

narration.script: Balance the formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen gas. Adjust the coefficients and watch the live atom count table.

keyIdeas: Atoms are conserved in chemical reactions; subscripts define the substance and must never be changed.

interactive.title: Balance the Formation of Water
interactive.instructions: Use the + and − buttons to set whole-number coefficients so hydrogen and oxygen atoms are conserved in the simplest ratio.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive chemical equation balancer for water formation
interactive.fallbackText: Balanced equation: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) (4 H atoms and 2 O atoms on both sides).

prediction.prompt: One molecule of O₂ provides 2 oxygen atoms. How many H₂O molecules must be formed to use both oxygen atoms?
prediction.explanation: Each H₂O contains 1 oxygen atom, so 2 H₂O molecules balance 1 O₂ molecule.

interactive.successExplanation: Balanced! 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l) conserves 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms in the simplest whole-number ratio (2 : 1 : 2).

slides.title: C02 · Chemistry — Haber Process Reversible Equation
slides.purpose: Balance a reversible industrial synthesis equation with a reversible arrow (⇌).
onScreenText: Reversible reaction arrow (⇌) indicates dynamic equilibrium
N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g)
Conservation balancing is separate from reaction conditions

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="210" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="36" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">C02 · Haber Process</text><text x="400" y="260" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="24" fill="#15803d">N₂(g) + H₂(g) ⇌ NH₃(g)</text></svg>

narration.script: Balance the reversible Haber process equation used to manufacture ammonia for fertilisers.

keyIdeas: Reversible equations obey the exact same atom-conservation rules as irreversible reactions.

interactive.title: Balance the Haber Process Equation
interactive.instructions: Balance nitrogen and hydrogen atoms across the reversible reaction arrow.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive chemical equation balancer for the Haber process
interactive.fallbackText: Balanced equation: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) (2 N atoms and 6 H atoms on both sides).
interactive.modelNote: Atom conservation verifies stoichiometry only; actual industrial ammonia synthesis requires an iron catalyst, ~450 °C, and ~200 atm.
interactive.successExplanation: Balanced! N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) conserves 2 N atoms and 6 H atoms in the simplest ratio (1 : 3 : 2).

slides.title: C03 · Chemistry — Parenthesised Compound Neutralisation
slides.purpose: Count atoms accurately inside parenthesised chemical formulae such as Ca(OH)₂.
onScreenText: Ca(OH)₂ contains 1 Ca, 2 O, and 2 H atoms
Parenthesis subscript multiplies every element inside the brackets
Acid + alkali neutralisation forms salt and water

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fefce8"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#713f12">C03 · Parenthesised Formulae</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#a16207">Ca(OH)₂(aq) + HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + H₂O(l)</text></svg>

narration.script: Balance the neutralisation of calcium hydroxide with hydrochloric acid, taking care to count both oxygen and hydrogen inside the OH brackets.

keyIdeas: A subscript outside parentheses multiplies every element inside the parentheses.

interactive.title: Balance Ca(OH)₂ + HCl Neutralisation
interactive.instructions: Remember that Ca(OH)₂ has 2 O atoms and 2 H atoms. Balance all four elements.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive chemical equation balancer for calcium hydroxide and hydrochloric acid
interactive.fallbackText: Balanced equation: Ca(OH)₂(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l) (1 Ca, 2 O, 4 H, 2 Cl on both sides).
hints: Start by balancing chlorine (Cl) on both sides, then check total hydrogen and oxygen.
interactive.successExplanation: Balanced! Ca(OH)₂(aq) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + 2H₂O(l) conserves Ca, O, H, and Cl.

slides.title: C04 · A-Level Chemistry — Ionic & Redox Half-Equation
slides.purpose: Conserve both atoms AND total electric charge in an electrolysis oxidation half-equation.
onScreenText: Ionic half-equations must conserve both atoms and net charge
Anode oxidation of bromide ions: 2Br⁻(l) → Br₂(g) + 2e⁻
Each electron (e⁻) carries a charge of −1

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fdf2f8"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#831843">C04 · Redox Half-Equation</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="24" fill="#be185d">Br⁻(l) → Br₂(g) + e⁻</text></svg>

narration.script: Balance the anode oxidation half-equation for molten bromide ions, making sure both bromine atoms and total electric charge match on both sides.

keyIdeas: Half-equations require both atom conservation and total electric charge conservation.

interactive.title: Balance the Anode Oxidation Half-Equation
interactive.instructions: Balance both bromine atoms and net electric charge using Br⁻, Br₂, and electrons (e⁻).
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive ionic half-equation balancer for bromide oxidation
interactive.fallbackText: Balanced half-equation: 2Br⁻(l) → Br₂(g) + 2e⁻ (2 Br atoms and −2 total charge on each side).
interactive.modelNote: Represents the anode oxidation half-equation during electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide (PbBr₂) at high temperature (~370–400 °C), well above bromine's boiling point (58.8 °C), which is why bromine is evolved as a brown gas Br₂(g) rather than liquid Br₂(l).
interactive.successExplanation: Balanced! 2Br⁻(l) → Br₂(g) + 2e⁻ conserves 2 Br atoms and a net electric charge of −2 on each side.

slides.title: C05 · Physics — Series Electrical Circuit
slides.purpose: Build a closed 12 V series circuit with two 6 Ω lamps and verify V = IR and voltage division.
onScreenText: Series resistance adds: R_total = R₁ + R₂
Same current flows through every component in series
Potential difference divides across series loads (KVL)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#0f172a"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="34" font-weight="bold" fill="#38bdf8">C05 · Series DC Circuit</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#fbbf24">12 V · R_total = R₁ + R₂ · I = V / R</text></svg>

narration.script: Close the main switch and place two 6-ohm lamps in series with the 12-volt supply. Observe how the ammeter reads 1.00 amp and the voltmeter across one lamp reads 6.00 volts.

keyIdeas: In a series circuit, current is identical everywhere and supply voltage divides across the loads.

interactive.title: Build a 12 V Series Two-Lamp Circuit
interactive.instructions: Close the switch and place two 6 Ω lamps in Series Slots 1 and 2 so main current is 1.00 A and Lamp 1 reads 6.00 V.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive 12 volt DC series electrical circuit builder
interactive.fallbackText: With a closed switch and two 6 Ω lamps in series on a 12 V supply, R_eq = 12 Ω, I = 1.00 A, and each lamp has 6.00 V across it (P = 6.00 W).

goal.description: 2 lamps in series, I_total = 1.00 A, V across Slot 1 = 6.00 V

interactive.successExplanation: Verified! Two 6 Ω lamps in series give R_eq = 12 Ω, so I = 12 V / 12 Ω = 1.00 A and each lamp receives 6.00 V (KVL: 6 V + 6 V = 12 V).

slides.title: C06 · Physics — Parallel Electrical Circuit
slides.purpose: Verify Kirchhoff's Current Law (I_total = I_A + I_B) and independent branch switching in a 6 V parallel circuit.
onScreenText: Each parallel branch receives the full 6 V supply voltage
Total current equals sum of branch currents: I_total = I_A + I_B
Opening one branch leaves the other branch lit

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#0f172a"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="34" font-weight="bold" fill="#34d399">C06 · Parallel DC Circuit</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#a7f3d0">6 V · I_total = I_A + I_B · 1/R_eq = 1/R_A + 1/R_B</text></svg>

narration.script: Build a 6-volt parallel circuit with a 6-ohm lamp in each branch and compare the branch currents with the main-line ammeter reading.

keyIdeas: Adding a parallel branch lowers equivalent resistance and increases total supply current.

interactive.title: Build a 6 V Parallel Two-Lamp Circuit
interactive.instructions: Place a 6 Ω lamp in Branch A and a 6 Ω lamp in Branch B so each branch draws 1.00 A and total current is 2.00 A.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive 6 volt DC parallel electrical circuit builder
interactive.fallbackText: With two 6 Ω lamps in parallel across 6 V, each branch draws 1.00 A, total current is 2.00 A, and equivalent resistance is 3.00 Ω.

goal.description: Two 6 Ω lamps in parallel (I_A = 1.00 A, I_B = 1.00 A, I_total = 2.00 A)

interactive.successExplanation: Verified! Both 6 Ω parallel branches receive 6.00 V, each draws 1.00 A, and KCL holds: I_total = 1.00 A + 1.00 A = 2.00 A (R_eq = 3.00 Ω).

interactive.title: Mixed Series-Parallel Reference Circuit (12 V · 2 Ω + 6 Ω ∥ 6 Ω)
interactive.instructions: Place a 2 Ω resistor in the main series loop and two 6 Ω resistors in parallel Branches A and B, then verify R_eq = 5.00 Ω, I_total = 2.40 A, V_parallel = 7.20 V, and I_A = I_B = 1.20 A.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive 12 volt mixed series-parallel electrical circuit builder
interactive.fallbackText: In a 12 V mixed circuit with a 2 Ω series resistor feeding two parallel 6 Ω resistors, R_parallel = 3 Ω, R_eq = 5 Ω, I_total = 2.40 A, V_series = 4.80 V, V_parallel = 7.20 V, and each parallel branch carries 1.20 A.

goal.description: R_eq = 5.00 Ω, I_total = 2.40 A, V_parallel = 7.20 V, I_A = I_B = 1.20 A

interactive.successExplanation: Verified! R_parallel = 3.00 Ω + 2.00 Ω series = 5.00 Ω total; I_total = 2.40 A splits evenly (1.20 A each) across the parallel 6 Ω branches at 7.20 V (KVL: 4.80 V + 7.20 V = 12.00 V).

slides.title: C07 · Physics — Meter Connections & Short-Circuit Troubleshooting
slides.purpose: Diagnose and repair an intentional short circuit and a misplaced voltmeter in a troubleshooting circuit.
onScreenText: Intentional troubleshooting activity: fix the starting wiring faults
Ammeter goes in SERIES; Voltmeter goes in PARALLEL
Never bridge a supply with zero-resistance wire (short circuit)

visual.description: Fixing meter misconnections and short circuits.
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#450a0a"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#fca5a5">C07 · Meter & Short-Circuit Lab</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="20" fill="#fecaca">Diagnose the Faulty Wiring & Restore Safe Measurement</text></svg>

narration.script: This circuit starts with an intentional wiring fault: a short-circuit wire in Branch B. Replace the short-circuit wire with a 6-ohm resistor and ensure the meters are placed correctly.

keyIdeas: A zero-resistance path across a supply causes a short circuit; voltmeters belong in parallel and ammeters in series.
slides.teacherNote: Step 4D Preview Pilot C07 of 12 (intentional misconception/troubleshooting).

interactive.title: Fix the Short Circuit & Meter Misconnection
interactive.instructions: The starting circuit has a plain wire shorting Branch B and a misplaced ammeter in the parallel probe. Replace Branch B with a 6 Ω resistor and place the Voltmeter in the parallel probe.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive electrical circuit troubleshooting lab for short circuits and meter placement
interactive.fallbackText: Replacing the short-circuit wire in Branch B with a 6 Ω resistor and placing the voltmeter in the parallel probe restores safe operation (I_total = 2.00 A, V_probe = 6.00 V).

goal.description: Eliminate short circuit & meter faults (I_total = 2.00 A, V_probe = 6.00 V)

interactive.successExplanation: Faults resolved! Both branches now have safe 6 Ω loads, the ammeter is in series (2.00 A), and the voltmeter is in parallel (6.00 V).

slides.title: C08 · Biology — DNA Complementary Base Pairing
slides.purpose: Assemble an antiparallel 5′→3′ complementary DNA strand using A–T and C–G pairing rules.
onScreenText: DNA strands are antiparallel (3′→5′ paired with 5′→3′)
Adenine pairs with Thymine (2 H-bonds); Cytosine pairs with Guanine (3 H-bonds)
Uracil (U) does not occur in DNA

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#ecfeff"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="34" font-weight="bold" fill="#164e63">C08 · DNA Base Pairing</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#0e7490">3′–T A C G G A–5′  ↔  5′–A T G C C T–3′</text></svg>

narration.script: Build the complementary 5-prime to 3-prime DNA strand opposite the 3-prime to 5-prime template strand.

keyIdeas: DNA is antiparallel and follows strict complementary base pairing (A–T, C–G).

interactive.title: Build the Antiparallel Complementary DNA Strand
interactive.instructions: Select the complementary DNA nucleotide (A, T, C, or G) for each position along the 3′→5′ template strand.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive DNA complementary base pairing builder
interactive.fallbackText: DNA template 3′-TAC GGA-5′ pairs with complementary 5′-ATG CCT-3′ (A–T has 2 H-bonds, C–G has 3 H-bonds).
interactive.modelNote: Shows a 6-base DNA fragment; strands run antiparallel (3′→5′ paired with 5′→3′).

slides.title: C09 · A-Level Biology — DNA-to-mRNA Transcription
slides.purpose: Synthesise a 5′→3′ mRNA transcript from a 3′→5′ DNA template strand using Uracil (U) opposite Adenine (A).
onScreenText: RNA polymerase reads the 3′→5′ DNA template strand
mRNA is synthesised 5′→3′ (same sequence as coding strand, with U replacing T)
DNA Adenine (A) pairs with mRNA Uracil (U)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="34" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">C09 · mRNA Transcription</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#6d28d9">DNA 3′–T A C G A A–5′ → mRNA 5′–A U G C U U–3′</text></svg>

narration.script: Transcribe the 3-prime to 5-prime DNA template strand into a 5-prime to 3-prime mRNA strand. Remember that RNA contains uracil instead of thymine.

keyIdeas: Transcription reads the 3′→5′ DNA template strand to synthesise 5′→3′ mRNA with U instead of T.

interactive.title: Transcribe 5′→3′ mRNA from the 3′→5′ DNA Template
interactive.instructions: Build the complementary mRNA strand. Notice how the coding (non-template) DNA strand would have T where mRNA has U.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive DNA to mRNA transcription sequence builder
interactive.fallbackText: DNA template 3′-TAC GAA-5′ transcribes to 5′-AUG CUU-3′ mRNA (coding strand would be 5′-ATG CTT-3′).
interactive.modelNote: RNA polymerase uses the 3′→5′ DNA template (antisense) strand to build 5′→3′ mRNA; the opposite 5′→3′ DNA strand is the coding (sense) strand.

slides.title: C10 · A-Level Biology — Translation & Amino Acid Sequencing
slides.purpose: Translate 5′→3′ mRNA codons into an N- to C-terminus polypeptide, terminating cleanly at STOP without assigning an amino acid.
onScreenText: AUG = Start codon (Met); UAA/UAG/UGA = STOP (no amino acid)
Polypeptide grows from N-terminus (amino) to C-terminus (carboxyl)
Peptide bonds form by condensation reactions releasing H₂O

visual.description: Ribosomal translation of codons to polypeptide.
visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdfa"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#134e4a">C10 · mRNA Translation</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#0f766e">5′–AUG GGA UUU UAA–3′ → N–Met–Gly–Phe–C (STOP)</text></svg>

narration.script: Translate each 5-prime to 3-prime mRNA codon into its amino acid from N-terminus to C-terminus, and mark the UAA stop codon as STOP without assigning an amino acid.

keyIdeas: Stop codons terminate translation and do not code for an amino acid; amino acids join via condensation peptide bonds.

interactive.title: Translate mRNA Codons into a Polypeptide
interactive.instructions: Use the standard genetic code: AUG = Met, GGA = Gly, UUU = Phe, UAA = STOP (termination signal, no amino acid).
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive mRNA translation and amino acid sequence builder
interactive.fallbackText: 5′-AUG GGA UUU UAA-3′ translates to N-Met–Gly–Phe-C (2 condensation peptide bonds) and terminates at the UAA STOP codon.
interactive.modelNote: Complete short coding sequence from AUG start codon to UAA stop codon. In simplified textbook stoichiometry, peptide bond formation is written as a condensation reaction between –COOH and –NH₂ releasing H₂O; in living cells during ribosome-mediated translation, amino acids are first activated onto tRNA (using ATP) and peptidyl transferase in the ribosome catalyses peptide bond formation between aminoacyl-tRNA and peptidyl-tRNA.

slides.title: C11 · Biology — Monohybrid Inheritance (Punnett Construction)
slides.purpose: Construct gamete pairings for Tt × Tt and interpret genotype/phenotype ratios strictly as probabilities under complete dominance.
onScreenText: Parental cross: Tt (Tall) × Tt (Tall) under complete dominance
Genotype probabilities: 25% TT, 50% Tt, 25% tt
Phenotype probabilities: 75% Tall : 25% Dwarf (3 : 1)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f7fee7"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#365314">C11 · Monohybrid Inheritance</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#4d7c0f">Tt × Tt → 25% TT · 50% Tt · 25% tt</text></svg>

narration.script: Complete the 2-by-2 Punnett grid by combining one gamete allele from each heterozygous parent, and note that ratios represent probabilities per fertilisation event.

keyIdeas: Mendelian ratios represent probabilities for each independent fertilisation event, not guaranteed counts in small samples.

interactive.title: Construct the Tt × Tt Monohybrid Punnett Grid
interactive.instructions: Select each square in the 2×2 grid and choose the offspring diploid genotype formed by the row and column gametes.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive monohybrid Punnett square builder for Tt by Tt cross
interactive.fallbackText: Tt × Tt yields genotype probabilities 25% TT, 50% Tt, 25% tt and phenotype probability 75% tall : 25% dwarf under complete dominance.
interactive.modelNote: Assumes a single autosomal gene with complete dominance (T = tall dominant over t = dwarf recessive) and independent gamete segregation.

slides.title: C12 · Computer Science — Declarative Boolean Circuit Construction
slides.purpose: Build a combinational logic circuit purely from declarative JSON (no TypeScript activity mapping) graded by functional equivalence.
onScreenText: Target function: X = A AND (NOT B)
Authored 100% in JSON via circuitConfig (no TS activity file)
Graded by functional equivalence via circuit-engine.ts

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#0f172a"/><text x="400" y="205" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="32" font-weight="bold" fill="#818cf8">C12 · Declarative Boolean Circuit</text><text x="400" y="258" text-anchor="middle" font-family="monospace" font-size="22" fill="#c7d2fe">Target: X = A AND (NOT B) · Truth-Table Graded</text></svg>

narration.script: Build a combinational logic circuit whose output X equals 1 only when A is 1 and B is 0. Any functionally equivalent gate combination is accepted.

keyIdeas: Declarative JSON circuit configurations reuse circuit-engine.ts with functional-equivalence truth-table grading.

interactive.title: Build X = A AND (NOT B) (Declarative JSON Circuit)
interactive.instructions: Add and wire gates so the live truth table matches Target X = [0, 0, 1, 0] for (A,B) = (0,0), (0,1), (1,0), (1,1).
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Interactive declarative Boolean logic circuit builder for A AND NOT B
interactive.fallbackText: Target X = A AND (NOT B): invert B with a NOT gate (G1), then feed A and G1 into an AND gate (G2). Outputs 1 only when A=1 and B=0.

circuitConfig.successExplanation: Functionally equivalent! Your circuit outputs X = 1 exclusively when A = 1 and B = 0.

summary.recapScript: You have tested all 12 Step 4D Construction Laboratory pilot activities across Chemistry, Physics, Biology, and Computer Science.
